AI Training.demand_side_pattern: AI labs and data vendors (e.g. Mercor, OneForma) post projects on their own contributor platforms; demand is project-based and matching is selective.
AI Training.notes: Selective: identity verification, credential checks, skills evaluation. Project availability varies.

repeatable_default.cadence: per project you are matched to and complete

AI Training.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, an AI data/training company that pays contributors for completed project work.
AI Training.work_available_default: Not guaranteed — project availability varies and matching to projects is selective.

App Referral.demand_side_pattern: No open market — demand is your own network: people willing to install the app and complete the qualifying actions.
App Referral.notes: Same honesty rules as Referral Bonus. Referrer usually must be an app user already.

repeatable_default.cadence: per successful referral, subject to program caps

App Referral.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, which pays user-acquisition bonuses for referred installs/signups.
App Referral.work_available_default: No guaranteed work — you earn only when someone you refer completes the qualifying actions.

Bank Bonus.demand_side_pattern: The bank itself is the buyer — it runs the promotion to acquire depositors. Find current offers on the bank's official promotions page; the catalog's verified_source_url is the ground truth.
Bank Bonus.notes: Capital gate: most require parking $1,000+ or direct deposits for months. State-specific offers are common — geo comes from requirements/catches. New-customer-only with exclusion periods is the norm.

repeatable_default.cadence: once per bank per lifetime (or per the exclusion period in catches)

Bank Bonus.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, a bank paying a signup bonus to acquire new depositors.
Bank Bonus.work_available_default: One-time per person per bank — not ongoing work. Each bank pays the bonus once.

Beta Testing.demand_side_pattern: Product companies post tests on the platform (e.g. betatesting.com); demand flows through the platform's invite system.
Beta Testing.notes: Invites are scarce: official terms say most users get 0-5 invites/month with no guarantees.
Beta Testing.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, a user-research platform paying for completed test sessions.
Beta Testing.work_available_default: No guaranteed tasks — invites depend on matching your profile; most users receive few or none per month.

Brand Ambassador.demand_side_pattern: The brand runs the program on its own site; demand is the brand's campus/community marketing needs.
Brand Ambassador.notes: Often volunteer/perks-oriented or selective; compensation terms are frequently unpublished — say so.
Brand Ambassador.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, which runs a student/brand ambassador program.
Brand Ambassador.work_available_default: Application-based; acceptance and continued participation are not guaranteed.

Brokerage Promo.demand_side_pattern: The brokerage itself is the buyer — it pays to acquire funded accounts. Current offers live on the brokerage's official promotions page.
Brokerage Promo.notes: Capital gate is the whole game: tiers scale with deposit size (often $1,000s-$100,000s). Funds must usually remain for months/years to keep the bonus.
Brokerage Promo.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, a brokerage paying a funding bonus to acquire new accounts.
Brokerage Promo.work_available_default: One-time per person per brokerage — not ongoing work.

Business Banking.demand_side_pattern: The bank itself is the buyer, acquiring business deposits. Offers live on the bank's official business promotions page.
Business Banking.notes: Business-only gate plus large balance requirements (e.g. $25,000 for 90 consecutive days). In-person opening is common.
Business Banking.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, a bank paying a bonus to acquire new business checking accounts.
Business Banking.work_available_default: One-time per business per bank — not ongoing work.

Buyback.demand_side_pattern: The buyback company itself is the buyer (e.g. buybackboss.com, sellcell.com); it resells or recycles the devices.
Buyback.notes: 'Up to' prices assume top condition/storage/unlocked — say who_qualifies must OWN the device. Follow Buyback/Resale completed examples.

repeatable_default.cadence: per device you own and sell

Buyback.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, a device buyback company that resells or recycles the phones it buys.
Buyback.work_available_default: Always available while the buyer publishes prices — but you can only sell devices you actually own.

Cashback.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, a cashback platform that shares the affiliate commission merchants pay it.
Cashback.work_available_default: Only when you shop through the platform — this is a rebate on spending, not earnings.

Cashback/Shopping.notes: Cashback is a rebate on spending, NOT income. Minimums ($10 common), return windows (90 days), and monthly fees on some platforms — pull from catches.
Cashback/Shopping.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, a cashback platform that shares the affiliate commission merchants pay it.
Cashback/Shopping.work_available_default: Only when you shop through the platform — this is a rebate on spending, not earnings.

Code Bounties.demand_side_pattern: The company runs the bounty program on its own security page (e.g. MSRC); demand is the company's need for vulnerability reports.

Code Bounties.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, which pays bounties for accepted vulnerability reports.
Code Bounties.work_available_default: Reports always accepted, but only novel, in-scope vulnerabilities earn — duplicates earn nothing.

Crypto Reward.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, a crypto exchange funding a learn-and-earn or signup promotion.

Rebate/Incentive.demand_side_pattern: The utility or program administrator (e.g. Mass Save sponsors like National Grid) funds the rebate; demand is the program's energy-efficiency goals in its service territory.
Rebate/Incentive.notes: Gates: must be a residential customer of that specific utility, often moderate-income qualified, often requires installing qualifying equipment (heat pumps) or a home energy assessment. Payout timelines are frequently unpublished — say so.
Rebate/Incentive.work_available_default: Available while the program runs, but only to qualifying utility customers — typically homeowners installing qualifying equipment.

Receipt/Loyalty.demand_side_pattern: The brand's loyalty program (e.g. Pampers Club, Amazon Shopper Panel) rewards your purchase data and engagement.
Receipt/Loyalty.notes: Often 'no cash value' — points redeem for brand discounts, not cash. Expiry is common (e.g. 6 months). Invitation-only/waitlist programs exist — say so.
Receipt/Loyalty.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}'s loyalty program, rewarding your shopping data.
Receipt/Loyalty.work_available_default: Ongoing as you shop. Rewards are usually brand credit or small gift cards — not cash.

Recycling.demand_side_pattern: The retailer/recycler (e.g. Staples, inkrecycling) pays for returned cartridges; demand is their recycling/refill supply chain.
Recycling.notes: Payouts are store credit or small checks; minimums apply (e.g. 10+ cartridges or $15 value). Per-cartridge values are small ($0.25-$11.25).
Recycling.work_available_default: Available whenever you have qualifying items to recycle — volume-limited by what you actually have.

Referral Bonus.demand_side_pattern: No open market — demand is your own network: friends/family willing to open the account and complete the qualifying actions. Most people earn $0 from referrals.
Referral Bonus.notes: Referrer is usually an existing customer/member. The referred person must complete qualifying actions (join, deposit, transact) — the bonus is NOT paid for just sharing a link. Tiered/capped programs are common — pull caps from catches.

repeatable_default.cadence: per successful referral, subject to program caps

Referral Bonus.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, which pays referral bonuses to acquire new customers.
Referral Bonus.work_available_default: No guaranteed work — you earn only when someone you refer completes the qualifying actions; most people earn $0 from referrals.

Rent Assets.who_pays_pattern: Renters, via {Provider}'s platform (the platform takes its fee first).
Rent Assets.work_available_default: Listing-based; income depends on renter demand for your space — not guaranteed.

Signup Bonus.work_available_default: One-time per offer — not ongoing work.

Store Signup.who_pays_pattern: {Provider} (via its card issuer), paying a signup incentive.
Store Signup.work_available_default: One-time per person — not ongoing work.

Student Program.demand_side_pattern: The program provider (e.g. GitHub, textbook vendors); student-gated.

Student Program.work_available_default: Available to verified students while enrolled.

Survey.work_available_default: Survey-dependent — invitations are not guaranteed and depend on your demographic profile; screen-outs are common.

Telecom Promo.who_pays_pattern: {Provider}, a telecom carrier funding a subscriber-acquisition promotion.

Translation.work_available_default: You must find and win clients (ProZ) or pass verification and wait for orders (translate.com) — no guaranteed flow.

Tutoring.work_available_default: Session-based; hours are not guaranteed and depend on student demand for your subject.

UGC/Creator.work_available_default: No guaranteed earnings — campaign selection is competitive and affiliate earnings depend on your audience buying.

Unclaimed/Recovery.demand_side_pattern: State unclaimed-property programs (via NAUPA sites like missingmoney.com / unclaimed.org); the 'demand' is your own forgotten money, if any exists.
Unclaimed/Recovery.notes: Most searches return NOTHING — NAUPA: 1 in 10 people have unclaimed property, 9 in 10 do not. Claim processing takes weeks to months. Never use third-party finder firms that take a cut.

repeatable_default.cadence: whenever unclaimed property exists in your name (rare)

Unclaimed/Recovery.who_pays_pattern: The state's unclaimed-property program holding your funds.
Unclaimed/Recovery.work_available_default: Only if unclaimed property exists in your name — most searches return no match.
